//rewrites: SPA REWRITE — the single most important line of this file.
Without it, refreshing /admin or sharing a link to /login gives a 404,
because the browser asks Vercel for a file at that path and no such file
exists. With it, Vercel serves index.html for any path that is not a real
file, and React Router resolves the URL client-side. This is a REWRITE, not
a redirect: the URL in the browser does not change, which is what keeps the
browser's back button and relative links working.
//apiProxy: Set VITE_API_URL=/api and the frontend calls /api/... on its own origin.
Vercel then forwards those requests to the gateway (configure the same
rewrites entry in the Vercel dashboard under Settings -> Rewrites).
The benefit: the browser makes a SAME-ORIGIN request, so CORS disappears
from the picture entirely — no preflight, no Access-Control-Allow-Origin,
and no risk of the gateway's allowed-origins list drifting out of date.
The cost: one extra network hop through Vercel's edge on every API call,
and the gateway must allow the Vercel origin anyway for non-proxied calls.
Both approaches are supported. The direct-to-gateway setup (VITE_API_URL set
to the full https://...onrender.com URL) is what this project ships with,

Vite fingerprints filenames (index-a1b2c3.js), so these files can be cached forever. index.html must NOT be, or a deploy would never reach returning visitors.
